title: Everything works with just a keyboard
why: Some people can't use a mouse. They rely on the keyboard or on devices that act like one.
how_to_check: Set your mouse aside.
Press Tab to move forward and Shift+Tab to move back through the page.
Try to open every menu, button, dialog, and form using Enter, Space, and the arrow keys.
pass_looks_like: You can reach and use every control, and nothing needs a mouse hover or click to work.
common_fixes: Use real buttons and links instead of clickable divs. If you build a custom control, add keyboard handling for Enter and Space.

title: You can always see where the keyboard focus is
why: Keyboard users need to know which element is active, the way mouse users can see their cursor.
how_to_check: Press Tab through the whole page.
Watch for a clear outline or highlight on each item as you land on it.
pass_looks_like: Every focused item has a visible, easy-to-spot indicator.
common_fixes: Don't remove outlines with 'outline: none' unless you replace them with something just as clear.

title: Focus never gets stuck
why: If keyboard focus gets trapped in a widget, a keyboard user can't leave it.
how_to_check: Tab into every dialog, menu, video player, and embedded widget.
Check that you can always Tab or press Escape to get out.
pass_looks_like: You can always move focus away from any part of the page.
common_fixes: Make dialogs closable with Escape, and return focus to the button that opened them.

title: Tab order follows the page in a sensible order
why: A jumpy tab order makes it hard to follow what's going on, especially with a screen reader.
how_to_check: Press Tab through the page from the top.
Check the order matches how you'd read it: top to bottom, left to right.
pass_looks_like: Focus moves in an order that matches the visual layout and meaning.
common_fixes: Fix the order in the HTML itself. Avoid positive tabindex values.

title: There is a way to skip repeated navigation
why: Without it, keyboard users must Tab through the same menu on every page before reaching the content.
how_to_check: Load the page and press Tab once.
Look for a 'Skip to content' link, or check the page has proper landmarks (header, nav, main).
pass_looks_like: A skip link or clear landmarks let you jump straight to the main content.
common_fixes: Add a 'Skip to main content' link as the first focusable item and use a <main> element.

title: Links make sense in their context
why: Screen reader users often browse a list of links. 'Click here' tells them nothing.
how_to_check: Read each link's text together with the sentence, paragraph, list item, or table cell it sits in.
Ask: can I tell where this link goes from that?
Link text that makes sense on its own is even better.
pass_looks_like: Each link's purpose is clear from its text, or from its text plus the sentence, list item, or table cell around it.
common_fixes: Replace 'click here' and 'read more' with specific text, or add hidden text that completes the meaning.

title: Image descriptions are actually useful
why: A scan can tell you an image has alt text, but not whether it's any good.
how_to_check: Check each meaningful image's alt text.
Ask: if the image disappeared, would this text give the same information?
Check decorative images have empty alt text (alt="").
pass_looks_like: Meaningful images have short, accurate descriptions and decorative ones are skipped.
common_fixes: Describe the purpose, not the file name. Use empty alt for pure decoration.

title: Headings, lists, and tables are marked up properly
why: Screen readers use structure to let people skim and jump around.
how_to_check: Check that text that looks like a heading is marked up as a heading (h1 to h6), and that the levels follow a logical outline.
Check lists use real list elements and data tables use real table headers.
pass_looks_like: The page's visual structure matches its HTML structure.
common_fixes: Use heading levels for meaning, not size. Use CSS for looks.

title: Color is never the only way to show something
why: People with color blindness or low vision can miss meaning that's only shown by color.
how_to_check: Find places color carries meaning: errors, required fields, chart lines, selected states.
Check there's also text, an icon, or a pattern.
pass_looks_like: Information is still clear in grayscale.
common_fixes: Add text labels or icons next to color cues, and underline links in body text.

title: Text can be enlarged to 200% without breaking
why: Many people zoom text to read comfortably.
how_to_check: Zoom the browser to 200% (Ctrl/Cmd and +).
Check nothing is cut off, overlapping, or missing.
pass_looks_like: All content and functions are still available at 200%.
common_fixes: Use relative units like rem and avoid fixed heights on text containers.

title: The page fits a narrow screen without sideways scrolling
why: People who zoom a lot, or use small screens, shouldn't have to scroll in two directions to read.
how_to_check: Make the window about 320 pixels wide, or zoom to 400% on a wide screen.
Check the content fits one column and you only scroll up and down.
pass_looks_like: No horizontal scrolling for normal content. Tables and maps may be an exception.
common_fixes: Use responsive layouts and let long text and images wrap or shrink.

title: Videos with sound have captions
why: Deaf and hard-of-hearing users need captions to follow along.
how_to_check: Play each prerecorded video.
Turn captions on and check they match the speech and important sounds.
pass_looks_like: Captions exist and are accurate.
common_fixes: Add caption tracks. Don't rely on auto-captions without checking them.

title: Moving or blinking content can be paused
why: Motion can be distracting or make reading impossible for some people.
how_to_check: Look for carousels, auto-playing video, and animations that run longer than five seconds.
Check each one has a pause, stop, or hide control.
pass_looks_like: Anything that moves for more than five seconds can be paused.
common_fixes: Add a visible pause button and respect the prefers-reduced-motion setting.

title: Sticky bars don't cover the focused item
why: A sticky header or cookie banner can hide the element you just tabbed to.
how_to_check: Tab through the page with any sticky headers, footers, or banners showing.
Check the focused item is never completely hidden behind them.
pass_looks_like: A focused item is always at least partly visible.
common_fixes: Add scroll padding (scroll-padding-top) so focused items scroll clear of sticky bars.

title: Buttons and links are big enough to tap
why: Small, tightly packed targets are hard to hit with a finger, a tremor, or a mouse.
how_to_check: Check buttons and icon links are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or have enough space around them.
Pay attention to icon-only buttons and links in dense lists.
pass_looks_like: Each target is at least 24 by 24 pixels. Or, if it is smaller, a 24 pixel circle centered on it does not overlap another target or another small target's circle.
common_fixes: Increase padding on small controls. Links inside a sentence are exempt.

title: Anything you drag can also be done with a click or tap
why: Dragging is hard or impossible for many people.
how_to_check: Find drag-and-drop, sliders, and sortable lists.
Check there is another way to do the same thing with single clicks or taps.
pass_looks_like: Every drag action has a simple alternative.
common_fixes: Add up and down buttons to reorder, or click-to-place options.

title: Help is in the same place on every page
why: People who struggle to find help shouldn't have to hunt for it on each page.
how_to_check: If the site offers contact info, chat, or an FAQ link, visit a few pages.
Check it appears in the same spot and order each time.
pass_looks_like: Help options are in a consistent location across pages.
common_fixes: Put help links in the shared header or footer.

title: People don't have to re-enter the same information
why: Retyping is tiring and error-prone, especially for people with memory or motor difficulties.
how_to_check: Walk through a multi-step form or checkout.
Check info you already gave isn't asked for again, or is filled in for you.
pass_looks_like: Previously entered details are reused or easy to select.
common_fixes: Pre-fill fields or offer a 'same as above' option. Security re-entry like password confirmation is allowed.

title: Logging in doesn't depend on memory or puzzles
why: Remembering passwords or solving puzzles is hard for people with cognitive disabilities.
how_to_check: Try the login flow.
Check you can paste into password fields and use a password manager.
Check there's no puzzle or transcription test without an alternative.
pass_looks_like: Sign-in works with paste, a password manager, or another simple method.
common_fixes: Don't block paste. Offer email links, passkeys, or other alternatives to puzzles.

title: Form errors are described in text
why: People need to know what went wrong and where.
how_to_check: Submit a form with mistakes on purpose.
Check the error says which field has the problem and what to fix, in words.
pass_looks_like: Errors are shown in text, near the field, and announced to screen readers.
common_fixes: Write clear messages, link them to the field, and don't rely only on red color.

title: Form fields have clear labels and instructions
why: Placeholder text disappears and isn't a label.
how_to_check: Check each field has a visible label.
Check any format rules (like date format) are stated before the field.
pass_looks_like: Every field has a visible label and needed instructions.
common_fixes: Use <label> elements tied to inputs. Keep placeholders as hints only.

title: Custom controls tell assistive tech what they are
why: A custom dropdown or toggle needs a name, a role, and a state for screen readers.
how_to_check: List any custom widgets: menus, tabs, toggles, sliders.
Turn on a screen reader and check each announces its name, type, and current state.
pass_looks_like: Custom widgets announce what they are and whether they're open, selected, or checked.
common_fixes: Prefer native HTML elements. Otherwise add the right ARIA role and state and keep them updated.

title: Updates like 'Saved' or 'Item added' are announced
why: Screen reader users can miss messages that appear without moving focus.
how_to_check: Trigger actions that show messages: saving, adding to cart, search results updating.
Turn on a screen reader and check the message is read out.
pass_looks_like: Status messages are spoken without the user having to hunt for them.
common_fixes: Put messages in a live region (role="status" or aria-live).
